note: Fits the money and the starting point, misses the profile and the premise. On income he clears the bar in practice rather than on paper — a railroad shift worker, not a business owner or physician, but he pre-framed the price at $5,000 with his wife, called $6,000 'in the ballpark', said 'it's not really the money that really is a deciding factor', and has already spent heavily on a basement gym. On not_deconditioned he is the opposite of the excluded case: 5'8" and 210 lb targeting 185, trains hard on every day off, and is anything but gym-averse. On good_to_great he qualifies — he is already fit for 70 and chasing leanness and mobility from a decent base. Where he falls outside is occupation, which the stated ICP tests directly ('they own their own business, or they're a physician, something along those lines'), and health-as-neglected-area, which is simply not true of him: health is the most attended-to thing in his life, and his history is prostate cancer with surgery and radiation, former diabetes and hypertension, sleep apnea and a healing pectoral tear. That is a managed medical history, not a neglected one. He is also 70, and the stated ICP has nothing to say about age at all. Two observations for the rollup. First, he pre-empted the ICP himself, unprompted and accurately — 'a lot of people during things like this have said, well, I don't think I can help you, Jerry, because they want the perfect candidate who looks like he's maybe in his 30s... because they always say they want an executive or something' — which suggests the stated ICP is being felt by prospects who fall outside it. Second, this call is another instance of the standing finding in icp.json that the stated ICP carries no clinical criterion: the criterion that should have governed this conversation is whether a post-prostatectomy 70-year-old with a weak pelvic floor and a healing pec is cleared for loaded ballistic kettlebell work, and no such criterion exists to fail.
